_what: Mutants that survive and that NO test can kill without lying about how the code is reached. Each entry names the code by its source TEXT rather than a line number, because line numbers drift and a stale entry must fail loudly rather than point at the wrong code. `mutants` is how many surviving mutants the entry accounts for; the ratchet subtracts it from the module's behavioural survivors to give `openGaps`, and a module is DONE when openGaps reaches zero. Adding a row here is a claim that must carry evidence — see `reason` and the section named in `source`.
_rules: An anchor must appear EXACTLY ONCE in its module, or the entry names the line too.
If the anchor no longer appears, the entry is STALE: re-triage it, do not edit the anchor to match.
Deleting the code is better than recording it here. Nine mutants left this ledger that way in 66ad43d8d.
This ledger may not be used to reach a threshold. It records what cannot be killed, not what we did not get to.

entries.reason: Stryker drops the `?.`, which would throw only if `prereq.install` were undefined. The type makes `install` optional so the compiler requires the `?.`, but a prerequisite without an install block cannot reach this line: getInstallSteps returns null for one, and the handler throws 'No installation steps defined' on a null plan before executeInstallSteps runs. Killing it would mean mocking getInstallSteps to return a plan for a prerequisite that has no install block, which the real collaborator cannot produce.
entries.decision: none — the `?.` is required by the type and correct as written

entries.reason: Deleting the empty-clipboard guard changes nothing observable: an empty string fails validateDaLiveTokenStrict on the next line and returns undefined by the other route. The only difference is one debug log line, and asserting log text is what the ratchet exists to refuse to reward.
entries.decision: none — the guard skips a pointless validation call and says what it means

entries.reason: The value never reaches anything. Every read of this.state.lastUpdated is inside saveState, nine lines after it has already been overwritten with new Date(). Nothing outside stateManager.ts reads the state file's lastUpdated. So the parse, the default and the Date construction are all discarded.
entries.decision: OPEN — either drop lastUpdated from the load, or keep it so the state shape round-trips and add a comment saying the value is deliberately unused

entries.reason: Removing the guard does not change the outcome. parsed is undefined, the next line reads a property off it, that throws, and the surrounding try/catch swallows it into exactly the same defaults the guard returns to. The only observable difference is which of two log lines is written.

A test that removed it never reaches this line — it gets the refusal instead, which is what happened when one was written. The version sync on this line is real and is tested; only the guard around it is unreachable.

anchors: this.debugLogger.error('[Auth] Quick authentication check failed', error as Error);
this.debugLogger.error('[Auth] Authentication check failed', error as Error);
entries.reason: Both authentication checks wrap their token read in a try/catch that logs, caches a brief negative and returns false. Neither catch can be entered: making the CLI config store throw does not reach them because the in-process reader has its own fallback and answers rather than propagating, and TokenManager.isTokenValid adds no catch of its own. Reaching the catch would mean replacing TokenManager, which the service constructs itself.
entries.decision: none — a defensive catch around an external read is correct even when the current collaborator cannot trigger it; the reader's fallback is not a contract
entries.note: The source note records 8 mutants across both catch blocks without splitting them between the two. The split is not known; the count is.

entries.reason: Stryker drops the `?.`, which would throw only if `projectUpdates.get(key)` were undefined. The two lines above set the key when it is absent, so by this line the entry always exists; the `?.` is there because Map.get is typed `T | undefined`. A test cannot reach the undefined case: there is no input to performComponentUpdates that skips the set. The grouping itself is tested (two selections on one project reach the updater twice and save once), so only the guard is unreachable, not the push.
entries.decision: none — the `?.` is required by the type. A rewrite (`const list = get(key); if (list) list.push(...) else set(key, [selection])`) would be fully killable, but is a style change to src, outside this batch's remit

entries.reason: Both `?.` guard the same value on one path that cannot make it undefined: `proj` is a project that entered componentProjectMap only through its own componentInstances entries, so `proj.componentInstances` is defined and the indexed instance exists; the optional `instance` parameter therefore always arrives as an object. The types demand both chains (`componentInstances` is optional on Project, `instance` optional in the signature), and the only caller of the private method is that loop. Killing them would mean handing the loop a project whose instances vanished between the two passes, which nothing can do.
entries.decision: none — a restructure that carried the instance alongside each map entry would remove both chains but leaks a field into the public MultiProjectUpdateResult shape; not worth it for two mutants

entries.reason: The 403, 5xx and catch-all throws are all caught by the same deliberate catch-all a few lines down, which logs at debug level and returns null, so every one of them produces the identical outcome (hasUpdate: false) and the only thing that differs is the wording of one debug line. The 404 branch differs from them only by staying silent, and that silence IS asserted; what is left of it (`true`: every non-OK status goes silent) again differs by the log line alone. Killing these means asserting log strings, which the ratchet exists to refuse to reward — the same triage as 2026-09-02, when the tests were deliberately not written. What IS pinned: a non-OK body is never read as a release, whatever the status.
entries.decision: OPEN product question, not a test question — graceful degradation means a rate-limited SC sees "no update" indefinitely, identically to being current, with only a debug line to say why. If the extension should ever say "I could not check", this is where that decision lives.
